summary: Burst policy handoff causes sustained 429 rejects for background archiver workers
description: Issue summary: Starting 2026-03-09 ~03:00 UTC, AtlasSearch reported recurring 429s from their background archiver fleet (bulk embedding + archival jobs). These jobs are low-priority and historically run smoothly with a separate burst allowance. After a recent burst-pool weighting change (priority-smoothing rollout), archiver workers began receiving sustained 429s despite console showing remaining tenant credits. Impact: Backlog of archival jobs, delayed data availability in customer index pipelines, and SLA degradation for the archiver subproduct. Environment: Dedicated pool for AtlasSearch in prod-us-west using dedicated ingress proxy and sidecar agent for warmup/health checks.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Deploy background archiver worker group using the archiver route (/v1/archiver/bulk) to the dedicated pool with priority=low. 2) Trigger a mass backfill of ~10k small embeddings (1-2KB payloads) from 50 concurrent workers. 3) Observe responses and rate-limit headers. 4) Toggle burst-pool-weighting to the new smoothing policy (same config used in rollout). 5) Repeat backfill; observe elevated 429 rate within ~2 minutes. Expected: background workers should be able to consume burst credits or be queued rather than be hard-rejected. Actual: rapid increase in 429 responses with X-RateLimit remaining credits >0 in console for tenant overall.

comments: Riley Chen (Support): Customer reports 20-30% of archiver requests returning 429s after config change. Console shows tenant credits but per-route rejects increase.

Ava Thompson (SRE): Reproduced locally with traffic generator. Observed sidecar health probes being counted against the same refill window as archiver requests. Hypothesis: handoff logic during burst-weighting rollout places background lane into shared token window temporarily.

Diego Martinez (Platform Eng): Found race in token-handoff codepath where probe-type requests lack probe flag and are treated as interactive, causing double-accounting when burst pool migrates. Drafting PR to add explicit probe tag and route-isolation guard.

Riley Chen (Support): Shared workaround provided to customer: enable per-route isolation for /v1/archiver/* and schedule backfills to off-peak hours while we patch. Customer accepted temporary schedule change.
Ava Thompson (SRE): Created alert for sudden spike in archiver 429s and added a dashboard tile for per-route refill headroom.
investigation_notes: Repro steps executed in staging using loadgen (50 workers, 1k requests/min). With new smoothing policy applied, refill handoff code briefly returns a transitional token-window id that reconciles counts incorrectly when sidecar probes fire concurrently. Root cause: sidecar healthcheck requests are not marked as 'probe' at the ingress layer during handoff, so they decrement the window token pool. When handoff completes, the pool is left with depleted per-route credits even though tenant-level credits remain. Intermittent nature explained by timing: only visible when handoff coincides with a probe burst (rolling deploys, k8s readiness probes). Reproduced on prod-dedicated replica. Correlated logs: token-window-id changes at handoff timestamps and repeated PREP health logs present. Metrics: per-route refill headroom drop correlates with 429 spike.
resolution: Short-term workaround: enabled per-route isolation for /v1/archiver/* for AtlasSearch and recommended scheduling large backfills to after midnight PST. Implemented traffic-class override to exclude healthcheck paths from token accounting. Long-term fix: merged PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/3821 to tag sidecar probes explicitly and added guard in token-handoff path to skip probe-type requests. Config rollout plan: staged on dedicated pools 2026-03-11 -> full rollout 2026-03-12 after smoke tests. Follow-ups: 1) Add unit test for probe-exclusion in token-handoff (ENG-1844). 2) Create runbook step to verify per-route refill headroom post-rollout. 3) Postmortem doc and customer-facing summary to be created in Confluence. Current status: fix merged and staged in prod for AtlasSearch; customer backlog draining, monitoring shows 429 rate returning to baseline.
